# Railway Gotchas

> Known Railway platform patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [`railway ssh` hangs on host-key verification in non-TTY shells](ssh-host-key-verification-hangs.md): `railway ssh --service X -- <cmd>` prompts to accept the host key and hangs forever in a non-interactive shell; use the system ssh client with StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new and BatchMode=yes after registering a key. MEDIUM.
- [Service source writes report "applied" and silently do not persist (checkSuites / Wait for CI)](service-source-write-reports-applied.md): the Railway agent's update tool accepts `{source: {checkSuites: true}}` and returns `"status": "applied"`, but the value never lands -- a fresh read still shows `false`, before and after committing staged changes; the agent's own read-back omits the key entirely, which invites the backwards inference that absence means success. Wait for CI is dashboard-only. Verify every config write by re-reading with the same read tool and quoting the field. HIGH.
- [`update-service` returns `updatedFields` echoing the REQUEST, so a partly-ignored write reads as a full success](update-service-updatedfields-echoes-request.md): `updatedFields` lists what you ASKED for, not what was written -- send three `deploy.*` fields, have one silently dropped, and all three come back with no error. Worse than the total-failure `source` case, because spot-checking one field and generalising is the natural defence and it fails: `preDeployCommand` and `restartPolicyMaxRetries` landed while `restartPolicyType` did not, and the read-back OMITTED the key rather than showing a wrong value, inviting "absence means it defaulted fine". Expensive because `preDeployCommand` is where deploy-time migrations run, so a phantom write means code ships against a schema missing its columns. Re-read and assert every field by name, treat a missing key as not-written, and cross-check with `railway config plan` for the EFFECTIVE value. Check the platform default first -- `restartPolicyType: null` is harmless (default IS ON_FAILURE) while maxRetries genuinely needed setting (default 10). Note Config as Code OVERRIDES service settings until it stops being read on 2026-12-01. HIGH.
- [`curl -I` reports `x-cache: DYNAMIC` on a URL the CDN caches perfectly over GET](head-request-reports-cache-dynamic.md): `curl -I` sends HEAD, and Railway's edge answers HEAD with `x-cache: DYNAMIC` even for URLs it caches correctly on GET -- so the natural way to check caching (headers only, hence `-I`) produces a confident FALSE NEGATIVE, identically on every retry, and the docs list "GET or HEAD" as cacheable so nothing warns you the diagnostic path differs from the served path. `DYNAMIC` is a substantive answer ("reached your service, couldn't cache"), which sends you to the skip-reason list that the response satisfies none of -- an immutable content-hashed JS chunk with `public, max-age=31536000`, no Set-Cookie and `Vary: Accept-Encoding` reads as a platform fault. Cost here: concluding "CDN is on but nothing caches, the toggle must not have saved" and toggling a CORRECT production setting off and on; the next steps would have been changing HTML caching mode or raising the TTL on evidence produced by the measurement. Use `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null` (a real GET) and judge the SECOND request: `MISS` then `HIT`, with `age` rising. One GET proves nothing, and a cache-buster query param reproduces the false negative by a different route since query strings are part of the cache key. With HTML caching on Never, verify BOTH halves -- assets `MISS`->`HIT`, HTML staying `DYNAMIC` -- because checking only the negative half cannot distinguish "HTML correctly not cached" from "CDN off entirely". HIGH.
